name: Simplification
why: Simplification questions appear directly (10-15 per Prelims) and form the computational engine for every DI and Arithmetic question.
concept: Simplify an expression using VBODMAS: Vinculum (Bar) → Brackets () [] {} → Of (%) → Division → Multiplication → Addition → Subtraction evaluated left-to-right.
keyFormulas: VBODMAS precedence order: Vinculum → () → of/% → ÷ → × → + → −
a/b + c/d = (ad + bc) / bd
Unit digit technique: check last digit when options have distinct endings
Digital Sum: Sum digits until a single digit (ignore 9s). If lhs ≠ rhs, option is eliminated.
commonTraps: Performing multiplication before 'of' (% of X)
Misinterpreting -a² vs (-a)²
Forgetting order of left-to-right divisions: a ÷ b ÷ c = (a/b) ÷ c = a / (b × c)

name: Approximation
why: Approximation explicitly asks for the 'closest value'. Exact calculation wastes precious seconds — strategic rounding is the test.
concept: Round each term to its nearest friendly baseline (nearest 10, 50, 100, or clean fraction equivalent) before multiplying or dividing.
keyFormulas: Compensating error rule: If you round one factor UP, round the other DOWN when multiplying.
commonTraps: Trying to calculate decimal places exactly
Over-rounding when option choices are tightly clustered (e.g., 142, 145, 148)

name: Missing Number Series
why: A guaranteed 5-question block in every Bank Clerk Prelims. 2-pass recognition allows securing 5 marks in 2.5 minutes.
concept: Determine the governing rule connecting terms: constant difference, double difference (2nd order), constant/growing ratio, n² ± k, n³ ± k, or alternating operations.
keyFormulas: Pass 1: Difference check (step 1 difference, if not clear check step 2 difference)
Pass 4: Alternating or Prime number additions (+2, +3, +5, +7, +11, +13)
commonTraps: Spending >45 seconds stuck on a single series instead of skipping and returning
Assuming addition when terms are rapidly growing (multiplication indicator)

name: Wrong Number Series
why: Frequently tested in IBPS Clerk & SBI Clerk to slow candidates down. Identifying the single faulty term requires verifying ripple effects across two differences.
concept: One term in the sequence violates the otherwise uniform rule. A single wrong term typically corrupts TWO consecutive difference values.
keyFormulas: Identify the two irregular differences — the common boundary term between them is almost always the culprit.
Re-calculate the expected term to confirm the remainder of the series restores consistency.
commonTraps: Picking the term after the faulty term without checking the forward connection

name: Quadratic Equations
why: Another guaranteed 5-mark block. With the Sign Method, 2 out of 5 questions can be answered in under 5 seconds without factorizing!
concept: Solve ax² + bx + c = 0 and dy² + ey + f = 0, then compare all roots of x with all roots of y to establish: x > y, x < y, x ≥ y, x ≤ y, or x = y / CND.
keyFormulas: Standard sign flip rule:
Equation (+, +) → Roots are (-, -)
Equation (-, +) → Roots are (+, +)
Equation (+, -) → Roots are (-, +)
Equation (-, -) → Roots are (+, -)
SUPER HACK: If constant terms in both equations are negative (c < 0 and f < 0), relationship is ALWAYS 'Cannot be determined (CND)'!
commonTraps: Forgetting to divide root factors by leading coefficient 'a' when a ≠ 1
Confusing x² = 64 (roots +8, -8) with x = √64 (principal root only: +8)

name: Percentage
why: The foundational language of all commercial arithmetic (P&L, SI/CI, Ratio, Partnership, DI).
concept: A fraction with denominator 100. Percentage change = (Change / Original) × 100.
keyFormulas: x% of y = y% of x  [Commutative property: 64% of 25 = 25% of 64 = 16]
Successive % change = a + b + (ab / 100)
Product constancy: If Price increases by 1/n, Consumption must decrease by 1/(n+1) to keep expenditure constant
commonTraps: Dividing by the final value instead of the original/base value when calculating % change

name: Ratio & Proportion
why: Replaces tedious multi-variable algebra with single-multiplier unit scaling.
concept: Comparison of two quantities of the same unit. If a : b = c : d, then product of extremes = product of means (ad = bc).
keyFormulas: Unit method: If ratio is 5 : 3 and difference is 20, 2 units = 20 ⇒ 1 unit = 10
Mean Proportional between a & b = √(ab)
Third Proportional to a & b = b² / a
Fourth Proportional to a, b, c = (b × c) / a
commonTraps: Adding absolute quantities directly to ratio components without converting to units

name: Average
why: One of the quickest arithmetic marks when solved via the Deviation (Net Balance) Method instead of total summing.
concept: Average = Sum of items / Number of items. Total sum = Average × Number.
keyFormulas: Net Deviation Method: Actual Avg = Assumed Avg + (Net Deviation / n)
Inclusion/Exclusion: Weight of new person = New Avg + (Change in Avg × Old Count)
Weighted Average = (n₁A₁ + n₂A₂) / (n₁ + n₂)
Average of first n consecutive natural numbers = (n + 1) / 2
Average of first n consecutive even numbers = n + 1
Average of first n consecutive odd numbers = n
commonTraps: Recalculating total sums from scratch when a new member replaces an existing one

name: Profit, Loss & Discount
why: Regular staple in both Prelims and Mains, linking CP, SP, MP, and Discount percentages.
concept: Profit/Loss is always calculated on Cost Price (CP) unless stated otherwise. Discount is always calculated on Marked Price (MP).
keyFormulas: CP / MP relation: CP / MP = (100 - Discount%) / (100 + Profit%)
Dishonest dealer profit% = [Error / (True Value - Error)] × 100
When two articles are sold at same SP, one at x% profit and other at x% loss, overall is ALWAYS a loss = (x/10)%²
Successive discounts d₁ and d₂: Net discount = d₁ + d₂ - (d₁d₂ / 100)
commonTraps: Calculating discount percentage on CP instead of MP
Assuming no profit/loss when SP is same and profit% equals loss%

name: Simple & Compound Interest
why: Direct test of percentage compounding. 2-year and 3-year CI-SI difference formulas save up to 2 minutes of calculation.
concept: SI grows linearly on Principal. CI grows exponentially on Principal + Accumulated Interest.
keyFormulas: CI Amount = P(1 + R/100)ᵀ
2-Year CI - SI Difference = P × (R / 100)²
3-Year CI - SI Difference = P × (R / 100)² × (3 + R / 100)
Effective rate for 2 years CI at r% = 2r + r²/100
Rule of 72: Doubling time in years ≈ 72 / Interest Rate
commonTraps: Using full annual rate R when compounding is half-yearly (use R/2 and 2T) or quarterly (use R/4 and 4T)

name: Time & Work
why: LCM / Efficiency method completely eliminates fractions and turns word problems into clean integer arithmetic.
concept: Total Work = LCM of individual times. Efficiency (units/day) = Total Work / Time. Combined Time = Total Work / Total Efficiency.
keyFormulas: Total Work = Efficiency × Time
M₁D₁H₁ / W₁ = M₂D₂H₂ / W₂  [MDH Formula]
Efficiency ratio is inversely proportional to time taken: If E_A : E_B = 3 : 2 ⇒ T_A : T_B = 2 : 3
Wages are distributed in the ratio of work done (or efficiency if time worked is same)
commonTraps: Adding days directly (e.g. 10 days + 15 days ≠ 25 days)
Miscounting days when persons join or leave midway through the project

name: Pipes and Cisterns
why: Time & Work with negative efficiency. Once you treat emptying pipes as negative rates, the logic is identical.
concept: Inlet pipes add capacity (+ve rate); outlet pipes remove capacity (-ve rate). Net Rate = Σ(Inlet rates) - Σ(Outlet rates).
keyFormulas: Tank Capacity = LCM(t₁, t₂, ...)
Net Filling Rate = (Capacity / t_in) - (Capacity / t_out)
Leak problem: If pipe fills in T hours and with leak takes T' hours, leak empties full tank in: (T × T') / (T' - T) hours
commonTraps: Adding outlet efficiency instead of subtracting it from the total rate

name: Time, Speed & Distance
why: Unifies linear motion, trains, boats, and races under Distance = Speed × Time.
concept: When Distance is constant, Speed ∝ 1/Time. When Time is constant, Distance ∝ Speed.
keyFormulas: km/h to m/s: multiply by 5/18; m/s to km/h: multiply by 18/5
Average Speed for equal distances: (2 × s₁ × s₂) / (s₁ + s₂)
Relative Speed (Opposite directions): s₁ + s₂
Relative Speed (Same direction): |s₁ - s₂|
Meeting time = Distance between them / Relative Speed
commonTraps: Averaging speeds directly as (s₁ + s₂)/2 instead of using harmonic mean when distances are equal

name: Problems on Trains
why: Direct application of Relative Speed with train lengths acting as distance.
concept: To cross a point object (pole, standing man), train covers its own length L. To cross an extended object (platform, bridge, tunnel, another train), distance covered = L₁ + L₂.
keyFormulas: Time to cross pole = L_train / Speed
Time to cross platform = (L_train + L_platform) / Speed
Time for two trains to cross = (L₁ + L₂) / Relative Speed
commonTraps: Forgetting to convert speed from km/h to m/s when lengths are in meters and time in seconds

name: Boats and Streams
why: Clean two-variable linear system. Downstream speed D and Upstream speed U yield boat speed B and stream speed S instantly.
concept: Downstream speed D = B + S. Upstream speed U = B - S.
keyFormulas: Speed of boat in still water B = (D + U) / 2
Speed of stream S = (D - U) / 2
Ratio B : S = (Time_up + Time_down) : (Time_up - Time_down) for equal distance
commonTraps: Confusing Downstream (+ stream) with Upstream (- stream)

name: Mixture & Alligation
why: The alligation cross rule solves weighted average and replacement problems without equations in 15 seconds.
concept: Ratio of Cheaper to Dearer quantity = (Price of Dearer - Mean Price) : (Mean Price - Price of Cheaper).
keyFormulas: Quantity_Cheaper / Quantity_Dearer = (Dearer - Mean) / (Mean - Cheaper)
Repeated replacement formula: Remaining original liquid = Initial × [1 - (x / C)]ⁿ, where x is quantity removed each time and C is total capacity.
commonTraps: Placing SP in the alligation cross when other values are CP (all three inputs must be on the same basis, e.g. all CP)

name: Partnership
why: High-scoring topic where profit ratio = Capital × Time ratio.
concept: Profit is distributed strictly proportional to effective investment: P₁ : P₂ = (C₁ × T₁) : (C₂ × T₂).
keyFormulas: Profit Ratio = (Capital A × Months A) : (Capital B × Months B)
Active partner salary is subtracted from total profit BEFORE splitting remainder in ratio
commonTraps: Forgetting to adjust capital when a partner adds or withdraws money after 3, 6, or 8 months

name: Problems on Ages
why: Extremely high accuracy topic. The key insight is that the difference between two persons' ages NEVER changes.
concept: Age difference remains constant across all years. Make ratio difference equal to bridge past, present, and future.
keyFormulas: Age difference (A - B) at any time t is constant
Ratio equalization: Multiply ratios by cross-differences to align unit passage of time
commonTraps: Adding x years to only one person instead of both when shifting from past to future

name: Permutations & Combinations
why: Tested heavily in Mains. The whole skill is distinguishing whether order matters (arrangement) or not (selection).
concept: Permutation ⁿPᵣ = n! / (n - r)! (Order matters). Combination ⁿCᵣ = n! / [r! × (n - r)!] (Order does not matter).
keyFormulas: ⁿCᵣ = ⁿCₙ₋ᵣ  [e.g., ¹⁰C₈ = ¹⁰C₂ = (10×9)/(2×1) = 45]
Arranging n items with repetitions: n! / (p! × q! × r!)
Items kept together: Tie them into a single super-item, arrange inside and outside
Circular permutation of n distinct items = (n - 1)!
commonTraps: Using permutation formula when only selection is required

name: Probability
why: Commonly asked in Mains and Clerk Prelims arithmetic. Standard questions involve balls in bags, playing cards, or coins/dice.
concept: P(E) = Number of favorable outcomes / Total possible outcomes.
keyFormulas: P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A ∩ B)
P(At least 1) = 1 - P(None)
Drawing without replacement: P(R₁ and R₂) = (r / total) × [(r - 1) / (total - 1)]
commonTraps: Calculating with replacement when the question specifies without replacement

name: Mensuration (2D & 3D)
why: Direct formula substitution. 95% of questions check cylinder, cone, sphere, rectangle, or circle.
concept: 2D: Perimeter and Area. 3D: Curved Surface Area (CSA), Total Surface Area (TSA), and Volume.
keyFormulas: Circle: Area = πr², Circumference = 2πr (For r = 7, Area = 154, Circumference = 44)
Cylinder: Volume = πr²h, CSA = 2πrh, TSA = 2πr(h + r)
Cone: Volume = ⅓πr²h, CSA = πrl (where l = √(r² + h²))
Sphere: Volume = (4/3)πr³, Surface Area = 4πr²
Semisphere: TSA = 3πr², Volume = ⅔πr³
commonTraps: Confusing CSA with TSA in hemisphere and cylinder problems

name: Tabular Data Interpretation
why: Carries 5-15 marks per exam. Fast row/column cross-referencing and percentage comparisons make or break your score.
concept: Data organized in rows and columns. Read headers and footnotes first, then compute differences, ratios, and percentages.
keyFormulas: % More/Less = |A - B| / Base × 100
Average = Row/Column Total / Count
Ratio A to B = Value(A) / Value(B)
commonTraps: Looking at the wrong row or year under exam stress

name: Bar Graph & Line Graph DI
why: Visual trend analysis. Checking axis scales and grid intervals allows immediate estimation of quantities.
concept: Bar heights or line peaks represent numerical values across categories or years.
keyFormulas: Growth Rate = (Value_Final - Value_Initial) / Value_Initial × 100
Visual subtraction: Count grid units between bars instead of reading and subtracting large numbers
commonTraps: Misidentifying axis scale markings (e.g. each line is 5 units, not 10)

name: Pie Chart DI
why: Angle to percentage conversion (360° = 100% ⇒ 3.6° = 1%) allows instant direct ratio answers without computing raw values.
concept: Distribution of a total 100% or 360° among distinct sectors.
keyFormulas: When comparing sectors of the same chart, compare degrees/percentages directly — NEVER calculate raw rupee/unit values first!
commonTraps: Converting each percentage into raw values before computing the ratio (wastes 45 seconds)

name: Caselet & Venn Diagram DI
why: Standard in Mains exams. Raw paragraph text must be decoded into a neat 2-way table or 3-circle Venn diagram.
concept: Unpack given clues into a Venn diagram: Only A, Only B, Both A & B, All three, None.
keyFormulas: n(A ∪ B) = n(A) + n(B) - n(A ∩ B)
Total = (Only A + Only B + Only C) + (A∩B only + B∩C only + C∩A only) + (All 3) + None
commonTraps: Confusing 'People who like A' with 'People who like ONLY A'

name: Quantity Comparison (Q1 vs Q2)
why: High-yield format in SBI & IBPS Clerk Mains. Tests two arithmetic concepts in one question and compares results.
concept: Evaluate Quantity I and Quantity II independently to choose: Q1 > Q2, Q1 < Q2, Q1 ≥ Q2, Q1 ≤ Q2, or Q1 = Q2 / Relation cannot be established.
keyFormulas: Always check edge conditions (zero, negative numbers, fractions between 0 and 1) when quantities involve powers or roots
commonTraps: Finding both values accurately but selecting the wrong relation sign in haste

name: Data Sufficiency
why: Unique topic where you DO NOT need to calculate the numerical answer! You only evaluate whether the given statements provide sufficient information.
concept: Test Statement I alone, Statement II alone, and then Statements I & II together to see if a unique answer exists.
keyFormulas: Step 1: Check Statement I alone
Step 2: Check Statement II alone
Step 3: If neither alone works, combine I + II
Golden rule: Stop solving the moment uniqueness is proven — never waste time on final calculation!
commonTraps: Accidentally carrying information from Statement I over when testing Statement II alone

name: Races & Games of Skill
why: Head start and beat-by problems convert directly into speed ratios.
concept: If A gives B a head start of h meters in a race of d meters, in the same time A runs d meters, B runs (d - h) meters.
keyFormulas: Speed Ratio A : B = d : (d - head_start)
If A beats B by t seconds, B's speed = distance_beaten / t
commonTraps: Confusing start in distance (meters) with start in time (seconds)

name: Clocks & Calendars
why: 100% formulaic. Once you know odd days mod 7 and |30H - 5.5M|, you score full marks in 30 seconds.
concept: Clocks: Angle between hands = |30H - 5.5M|. Calendars: Count odd days mod 7 across ordinary and leap years.
keyFormulas: Clock angle = |30H - (11/2)M| degrees
Hands coincide (0°): 11 times in 12 hours, 22 times in 24 hours
Hands in opposite direction (180°): 22 times in 24 hours
Ordinary year = 1 odd day; Leap year = 2 odd days
commonTraps: Taking an interior reflex angle (>180°) instead of the acute angle (subtract from 360°)

name: True & Banker's Discount
why: Bank-specific financial mathematics comparing true present worth interest with bill discount.
concept: True Discount (TD) is interest on Present Worth (PW). Banker's Discount (BD) is interest on Face Value. BD is always > TD.
keyFormulas: Amount = PW + TD
TD = (Amount × R × T) / (100 + RT)
BD = (Amount × R × T) / 100
Banker's Gain (BG) = BD - TD = (TD × R × T) / 100
Amount = (BD × TD) / (BD - TD)
commonTraps: Confusing Banker's Discount (BD) with trade discount in Profit & Loss

name: Surds & Indices
why: Simplifies huge exponential equations without multiplying powers out.
concept: Base alignment and power arithmetic rules.
keyFormulas: aᵐ × aⁿ = aᵐ⁺ⁿ
aᵐ ÷ aⁿ = aᵐ⁻ⁿ
(aᵐ)ⁿ = aᵐⁿ
a⁻ⁿ = 1 / aⁿ
a⁰ = 1
If aˣ = aʸ (a ≠ 0, 1, -1), then x = y
commonTraps: Applying power laws when bases are different without reducing to common prime base first

name: Square & Cube Roots
why: Instant recall of squares 1-50 and cubes 1-25 unlocks 10-second simplification.
concept: Direct unit-digit matching and nearest square/cube estimation.
keyFormulas: Unit digit of perfect square: 1→1,9; 4→2,8; 5→5; 6→4,6; 9→3,7; 0→0 (2, 3, 7, 8 NEVER end a square)
Base 50 squaring trick: For 50+x, answer is (25+x) | x²
commonTraps: Guessing square root without verifying the ten's digit against the lower square bound
